name: bayesian-calibration
title: Bayesian calibration: rate constants with honest uncertainty, not just a point estimate
question:
The recovery ladder fits a point estimate of the mass-action rate constants. Can
we instead recover a full posterior — the rate constants WITH calibrated
uncertainty — from noisy data, and is that posterior honest (does its 95%
credible interval actually contain the truth, and is it informative)?
hypothesis:
Mass-action is fully identifiable (recover-mass-action recovers it to nrmse ~1e-9),
so with a modest amount of noisy data the posterior over (k1, k2, k2r) should be
tight and centered on the truth: the 95% credible intervals should cover the true
values while being far narrower than the prior.
objective:
Generate noisy synthetic data from the known mass-action model, evaluate the
Gaussian likelihood on a grid over the three rate constants (an exact posterior,
no MCMC), and report the marginal posteriors, MAP, 95% credible intervals, and a
posterior-predictive check — graded on coverage and informativeness.
description:
A Bayesian extension of the recovery pipeline for the SBML-recovery investigation.
The calibration harness (viva_sbml_decomposition.harness.calibration) draws noisy
synthetic data from the mass-action oracle (A->B; A+B<->C; relative Gaussian
observation noise) and computes the EXACT posterior over (k1, k2, k2r) on a grid
under a uniform prior — no MCMC convergence to validate, fully deterministic given
the data seed. It reports the three marginal posteriors, the MAP, 95% credible
intervals, the prior widths, and a posterior-predictive band in observation space.

Wall-clock plays no role; the graded properties are reproducible: the 95% credible
intervals cover all three true rate constants (honest coverage), and each interval
is far narrower than the prior (the data is informative — a flat posterior that
trivially covers the truth would fail). Measured: MAP equals the truth to grid
resolution, every CI covers its true value, and each CI is ~10% of the prior
width. The committed baseline (visualizations/calibration_posterior.json) is this
machine's posterior. This turns recover-mass-action's point estimate into a
calibrated posterior — the recovery pipeline from estimate to uncertainty.

expected_behavior.name: posterior-covers-and-is-informative
expected_behavior.observable: 95% credible intervals for (k1, k2, k2r) from the grid posterior, vs the true values and the prior width
expected_behavior.condition: every true rate constant lies inside its 95% credible interval (coverage), and each interval is clearly narrower than the prior (informative — worst CI/prior width < 0.8)
expected_behavior.rationale: an honest Bayesian calibration must both contain the truth and be constrained by the data; a posterior that equals the prior would trivially "cover" the truth without learning anything.
